summary: Make a replaced Controller re-adopt everything the hosts hold: the Controller appliance VM from the appliance engine's deploy journal, failed and interrupted journal outcomes as task history, interrupted VM creations re-observed and promoted on the host, journaled VMs missing from libvirt flagged instead of adopted, one corrupt journal file no longer emptying the whole report, and no silent skips during adoption.

guide.reason: Replacing a Controller now brings back the appliance VM and the host's failed tasks, and shows what it could not adopt as needs_attention tasks plus two new host checks; the Replace a failed Controller troubleshooting entry and its verification paragraph describe this.

api.reason: API impact: changed contract. Inventory.managed (ManagedState) gains appliances, outcomes and missing_vms with the new Appliance and ManagedOutcome schemas; hosts report the managed-journal and managed-vms checks; Controller adoption records appliances rows, adopt-outcome operations and adopt-attention needs_attention operations with audit entries; the standalone agent takes --appliance-journal-dir. Protocol version and capability are unchanged: an older Core omits the new lists and a newer Controller adopts what it gets. POST /api/v1/appliances/adopt is unchanged and replays as already adopted once a report inserted the row.

state.reason: Every record a replaced Controller rebuilds here already lives on the host: the appliance engine deploy journal and the managed journal on the pool master. Controller rows (appliances, operations, audit) are mirrors rebuilt from host reports, plus Controller-scoped audit history.
state.record: Appliance ownership: the nex-core-local appliance engine deploy journal (<data-dir>/vmhost/<request_id>.json, /var/lib/nex/core-local/vmhost by default; Kind deploy, VMID, Name, ID=request ID), reported by the agent as Inventory.managed.appliances (vmhost.Deployments) and inserted into the Controller appliances table by adoptManaged on every managed report. Task outcomes and VM state: the managed journal (<agent-state>/managed-vms/<operation_id>.json) on the pool master, reported as Inventory.managed.outcomes, vms and missing_vms (ManagedEngine.Applied) and mirrored into operations/managed_resources by adoptManaged; interrupted creations are promoted in that journal by the host itself. Recovery path for a fresh Controller: enroll the pool master; its first managed report rebuilds all of the above.

verification.method: Go: go build ./... && go test ./... (all packages ok, including the new vmhost tests TestAppliedSurvivesCorruptJournalEntry, TestAppliedReportsOutcomes, TestAppliedPromotesInterruptedCreation, TestAppliedFlagsVMsMissingFromLibvirt, TestDeploymentsListsApplianceOwnership and the Controller test TestAdoptionRebuildsApplianceOutcomesAndAttention). The corrupt-journal regression test was run against the previous strict read and failed (state emptied), then passed with the fix. Contract: python3 scripts/generate_api.py and python3 -m unittest tests.test_api_contract (21 tests OK). Integration: tests/integration/controller_replacement.py extended to seed a deploy journal, a failed journal entry and a corrupt journal file on the host before Controller B starts; the namespace/no-VM variant from phase1.yml was run locally as root (result recorded in the bug ledger entry BUG-0065 and the commit message); the --vm variant (appliance re-adoption through real libvirt) was not run locally because this workstation has no libvirt.
